notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c) at head 3e3581d: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (the transcripts name only that model), uncommitted false and one skill_hash; each transcript contains the reworded do: sentence ("The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard"). Opus-1 read SKILL.md with Read and references/library-design.md with cat; haiku-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md with Read; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it, as the previous sweep counted opus-1's extra read. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.4). Doctests all pass: opus-1 2, haiku-1 2, haiku-2 1, sonnet-1 3, sonnet-2 3.

No rule in this case's list changed since 0397dec (git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches none of the nine sections), so every verdict follows the 2026-10-22-b grades' standard. The changes are outside the list: the defstruct sentence added to "Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}`" (no run writes `field: nil` in a defstruct), the do: rule's wrapped-line and `if` sentences (no run wraps a do: body; opus-1 line 227 and haiku-1 line 96 / haiku-2 line 151 keep `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` on the if's line), the new "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (not counted: sonnet-1 lines 136-143 and sonnet-2 lines 139-140 and 149-150 wrap a struct literal inside an {:ok, _} tuple, which is not a call argument; opus-1 line 174 and haiku-2 line 129 build the struct under a name first), the new module-order rule (every module has only alias lines, right after @moduledoc), Before you finish step 4, the How-to-use bullets, processes.md and testing.md.

Closest calls. Multi-clause heads: haiku-2 line 105, defp event_type(%{"type" => type}), do: {:error, {:unsupported_event, type}}, binds type with no guard and uses it only in the body; the key's presence selects the clause, so it is graded violated, as the previous sweep graded haiku-2's def parse(%{"type" => type} = payload), although this is the open-set catch-all that Match every expected shape asks to bind and name what it catches; had it been graded clean, Haiku would be clean on the rule. Struct rule: opus-1's Payments.Webhook.Error (line 75, defexception [:reason]) has @type t (line 83) but no @enforce_keys, and message/1 has no clause for a nil reason; the previous sweep counted the same shape (ParseError) as violated, so this is too, and it is opus-1's only break of a graded rule. Opus-1's Error.message/1 binds the reason tuple's element next to the tag that selects the clause (lines 86-93), not counted, as before.

Match every expected shape: haiku-2's event_type/1 catch-all (line 105) also receives a present non-string type, so "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} and "type" => nil gives {:unsupported_event, nil} (verified); the previous sweep's skill-haiku-2 had the same behaviour and put it in checks only, so it goes in checks here and the rule stays clean. The other four check the type with a string reader before the catch-all and return {:invalid_field, "type"}. Every `{:ok, _value} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, key}}` or `_value ->` clause in the five files follows a guarded success clause and receives only present values of the wrong type. data["failure_reason"] (haiku-1 line 65), map[key] (opus-1 line 204) and Map.get (haiku-2 line 159) read optional keys and are allowed.

Naming: haiku-2's fetch_field/3 (line 148) looks a key up, checks the value and returns {:error, {:invalid_field, key}}, the fetch_ case the rule names; no other run has a fetch_* or get_* function (required_field/3, optional_field/3, cast_*, string_field/2, amount_field/2, map_field/2, timestamp_field/2, datetime_field/2). Every variable named data holds the payload's "data" map. Not counted, as earlier grades did not count similar names: parsed_data (sonnet-1), event_data (haiku-2), details and email (sonnet-2), fields and header (haiku-1), type_name and cast_value (opus-1); the Event structs' data field is a struct field, not a variable.

Outside the case list: an if inside a case (haiku-1 line 96, haiku-2 line 151) goes under Keep functions short, as before; haiku-2's two parse_data/2 clauses (lines 115-121) wrap one-expression delegations in do ... end blocks, though either fits on the head's line with do: (82 and 64 columns), counted under the unchanged do: sentence "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head". The with rule: every with in the five files has two to seven steps, no else and no case in its body; a one-step case whose :ok branch calls another fallible function (opus-1 required_field/3 line 198, sonnet-1 datetime_field/2 line 197, sonnet-2 timestamp_field/2 line 180) is not counted, as before.

Probe of 25 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file: in all five, an unknown type gives an unsupported-event error, a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, a string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}, refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field, an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}, and missing or non-map data gives {:missing_field, "data"} or {:invalid_field, "data"}. Differences: a present nil amount is missing in opus-1 (as its Error @moduledoc says) and invalid in the others; a missing customer_email is accepted by opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 (optional by design) and rejected by haiku-1 and sonnet-2; a non-map payload raises FunctionClauseError in haiku-1 and haiku-2 and returns :invalid_payload in the others; an unknown type with no data gives {:missing_field, "data"} only in sonnet-2, which checks the type after the data.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-22-b at 0397dec): the with rule moves from Sonnet violated to clean (no one-step with in any run); Comments moves from Sonnet violated to clean (sonnet-1's doctest timestamp is now right, ~U[2024-09-22 10:13:20Z]); Naming moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-2's fetch_field/3); the multi-clause rule stays Haiku violated (haiku-2 again) and the struct rule stays Opus violated (an exception without @enforce_keys again).
